definition: The natural logarithm of a token's predicted probability, commonly used instead of raw probability for numerical stability and easier aggregation across a sequence.
details: Log probabilities are summed rather than multiplied across a sequence to compute overall sequence likelihood, avoiding the numerical underflow that would occur when multiplying many small probabilities together.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. Here is the short version: The natural logarithm of a token's predicted probability, commonly used instead of raw probability for numerical stability and easier aggregation across a sequence. The part that makes it sing: Log probabilities are summed rather than multiplied across a sequence to compute overall sequence likelihood, avoiding the numerical underflow that would occur when multiplying many small probabilities together. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. And that is Log Probability — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
